mechanism_narrative: When the Federal Funds Rate is persistently below its long-run average, the discount rate for future cash flows declines, lowering the present value of expected dividends and thereby driving positive S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from zero (p > 0.05) during the identified low-rate period.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in unemployment claims (PAYEMS) accompanied by a simultaneous decline in industrial production (INDPRO) signals weakening labor market strength and impending recession, leading to negative S&P 500 60-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by >10% while INDPRO decreases by >5% over the next month
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are positive in >70% of similar trigger events, or unemployment claims do not precede a sustained industrial production recovery.

mechanism_narrative: When consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) rises above 3% for two consecutive months, it anticipates a tighter monetary policy response, which compresses equity valuations and produces negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL crosses above 3.0 for two consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in >50% of similar inflation spikes, or FEDFUNDS do not rise correspondingly.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in industrial production (INDPRO) over three months indicates weakening supply-side capacity, reducing expected future earnings and generating negative S&P 500 5-day forward returns.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.05) during the INDPRO decline period.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in residential mortgage applications (HOUST) accompanied by falling unemployment (UNRATE) suggests a dual signal of demand recovery and liquidity easing, producing positive S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: HOUST increases by >15% while UNRATE falls by >0.2% over the next month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically significant (p > 0.05) in such dual-signal events.

mechanism_narrative: Persistent declines in monthly job openings (implied by UNRATE below 4% for two months) indicate soft labor market, which precedes a bearish S&P 500 60-day forward return in a slow-growth regime.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE remains below 4% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are positive in >60% of similar low-UNRATE periods.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden spike in retail sales (implied by PAYEMS) followed by a decline in manufacturing output (INDPRO) suggests demand expansion without supply catch-up, pushing S&P 500 20-day forward returns to the positive.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by >20% while INDPRO decreases by >5% in the same month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significant (p > 0.05) in analogous events.

mechanism_narrative: When the 3-month moving average of FEDFUNDS exceeds 5%, it anticipates future rate hikes that devalue equities, resulting in negative S&P 500 5-day forward returns.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not negative (p > 0.05) during such FEDFUNDS spikes.
